thread.title: Stock Market Update: Financials, Amazon Lead S&P 500 Rebound

title: Stock Market Update: Financials, Amazon Lead S&P 500 Rebound
text:
Financials, Amazon Lead S&P 500 Rebound 26-Nov-18 13:00 ET Dow +206.47 at 24491.32, Nasdaq +83.99 at 7023.18, S&P +24.54 at 2657.24
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 trades near session lows, up 0.9%, after trading as high as 1.5% earlier. is up 0.8%, the Nasdaq Composite is up 1.0%, and the Russell 2000 is up 0.9%.
Helping contribute to today's rally has been the expectations that the stock market was due for a rebound following short-term oversold conditions. Last week saw the S&P 500 lose its yearly gains. However, the market has tended to sell into strength as of late, and that's played out a bit today, pulling stocks from session highs.
The S&P sectors that have provided support are financials (+1.7%), consumer discretionary (+1.5%), energy (+1.4%), and communication services (+1.3%).
There is not much news to account for the strong showing in the heavily-weighted financials space, but it is worthy to point out that the sector has showed relative strength this quarter, losing 4.4% versus an 8.9% decline for the S&P 500.
Amazon (AMZN 1548.21, +44.94, +3.0%) and retailers, in general, have provided a boost for the consumer discretionary sector (+1.6%). have contributed to the solid showing today. The SPDR S&P Retail ETF (XRT 45.35, +0.47) is up 1.1%.
The information technology sector (+1.0%) has kept pace with the broader market, though Apple (AAPL 170.38, -1.90) has provided no support, as it has squandered an early gain of 1.5% and now trades lower by 0.8%. Interestingly, Apple is now only $6 billion dollars away from losing its spot as the S&P 500's largest company by market cap. Microsoft (MSFT 104.88, +1.81, +1.8%) currently holds second place.
Conversely, the industrials (+0.1%), utilities (+0.1%), real estate (-0.1%), and consumer staples (-0.2%) sectors have underperformed the broader market.
In other corporate news, General Motors (GM 37.75, +1.82, +5.1%) recently announced additional restructuring efforts to drive annual run-rate cash savings of approximately $6.0 billion by year-end 2020. GM will cut production in five plants in what will cost up to $3.8 billion pre-tax dollars, of which the majority will be incurred in Q4 2018 and Q1 2019.
Looking at other markets, U.S. Treasuries have ticked lower, pushing yields higher across the curve. The 2-yr yield and 10-yr yield are up two basis points each to 2.84% and 3.08%, respectively. Also, the U.S. Dollar Index has climbed back into positive territory with a gain of 0.1% to 96.99. Separately, WTI crude has jumped 2.1% to $51.50/bbl, bouncing back from over a 10.0% drop last week, to help support the oil-sensitive energy sector (+1.4%).
